title: Stop planner tools destroying and eliding state they report as intact
summary: Fix silent checklist destruction, a validation check that runs against rewritten content, and the prepare truncation that let a verified handoff ship incomplete.
description:
Current state:

Reported by a peer agent session working in /Users/antonio/projects/heca on 2026-09-15, after a phase handoff it had verified resume-ready turned out to be missing six facts a cold agent needed. Two live code defects, a wanted setting, a current design document, a binding pair previously conflated, and a confirmed by-design behaviour a future agent must not "fix" — all carried by the previous handoff precisely because no task holds them, all dropped by the new one. A human asking "are you sure it has full context?" is what caught it.

Every claim below was verified against the code in this repository before this phase was written. P103(F005) already fixed that session's payload-size complaints (handoff_show 59,823 -> 14,610 characters on heca P082) and the descriptionRef rejection (packages/plan-core/src/payload-fallback.ts now accepts three-segment paths). The defects here are the ones P103 did not touch.

Verified defects, worst first:

1. Replacing a task checklist silently destroys every tick and reports success. `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts:1614` does `task.checklist = checklist.map((item, index) => ({ ..., checked: false }))`, with `checked: false` hardcoded; `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:1724` does the same. Nothing matches existing items by id or title, so editing eight titles loses all ticks and the call returns `updated: true`. The reporter lost six ticks and noticed only because an earlier agent had warned them in a handoff. A tool that reports success while destroying durable state is the most damaging defect in this set. Note the tool descriptions already steer agents toward `planner-task-checklist-toggle/add/remove` for granular edits, but the destructive path stays available and silent.

2. Supporting-document validation runs against content that auto-externalization has already rewritten. In `refreshPhaseHandoff` (`packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts:3770-3790`) an oversized body is externalized and `effectiveInput.content` is replaced with `externalized.content`. Validation then runs on that rewritten body (`:3795-3802`), and `validateHandoffContextSync` (`packages/plan-core/src/handoff-context.ts`) asserts `input.content.includes(requested.path)`. If the document path lived in the portion moved into the external file, the check fails against a body the path is no longer in, and `HANDOFF_SUPPORTING_DOCUMENT_INVALID` fires on a document that was correctly linked. The reporter's workaround — drop it from the manifest, leave it in prose — worked because the manifest is what triggers the check. Their guess about backticks in list items was wrong; the cause is ordering.

3. `handoff_prepare` returns the existing handoff elided, and asks the agent to reconcile against it. The protocol says "reconcile every still-relevant detail from an existing handoff", but prepare hands back a copy whose sections end in `[Extended detail continues in the linked planner document.]`, one of them cut mid-word ("⚠️ **Ownershi"). Prepare neither inlines the externalized text nor lists the headings it elided. The facts the reporter dropped lived entirely in that externalized document. This makes the loss structural, not careless.

4. `reconciledExistingHandoff` is an unchecked boolean. The author asserts it; nothing verifies it. The only gate on the most loss-prone step in the protocol is the agent's own say-so. Prepare knows the prior capsule's sections and could name the ones absent from the new content.

5. Auto-externalization splits without regard for structure. `externalizeOversizedHandoffContent` cut the reporter's body mid-numbered-list, moving "What is left" and half of two other sections out. A rewrite at 7,996 characters was kept whole, so the threshold behaviour is correct; only the split point is not section-aware.

6. Tool results are enormous even on success. A `planner-task-update` echo measured 122,628 characters in this session's own use and had to be spilled to a file by the harness. The reporter saw a rejected oversized description come back as a 125,115-character error — diagnosing a too-large payload cost more context than the payload did. The size limit is not stated up front and successful updates echo the entire task.

Goals:
- Make a checklist replacement preserve tick state, or refuse rather than destroy it silently.
- Validate supporting documents against the content the agent actually submitted, not a rewritten one.
- Give prepare's caller the previous capsule in full, or make what is missing explicit.
- Replace the unchecked reconciliation boolean with something the planner can verify.
- Split oversized handoffs at section boundaries.
- Bound tool results and state payload limits before a call fails.

Systems and files in scope:
- `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts` (task update at :1614, handoff tools, result shaping)
- `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts` (task update at :1724, handoff tools)
- `packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts` (`refreshPhaseHandoff`, `preparePhaseHandoff`)
- `packages/plan-core/src/handoff-context.ts` (`validateHandoffContextSync`, `externalizeOversizedHandoffContent`, `auditPhaseHandoff`)
- `packages/plan-core/src/handoff-reply.ts` (the shared reply shaping added by P103(F005)/T408; new payload work belongs here, not in an adapter)
- `packages/plan-core/planner-skill.md` and generated plugin copies
- focused core, MCP, Pi and server regressions

Behaviors to preserve:
- The candidate-then-verify contract, persisted read-back hash verification, exact rollback, terminal-phase archive discovery.
- The 8,000-character capsule target and 24,000-character ceiling, and automatic externalization above the target.
- The payload reductions and the no-duplication invariant established by P103(F005), now pinned by `packages/plan-core/test/handoff-reply.test.mjs`.
- Harness-agnostic core per AGENTS.md rule 4: shaping and validation belong in plan-core, never duplicated per adapter.

Edge cases:
- A checklist replacement that renames an item — preservation by exact title match will not find it, so decide deliberately between id-based matching, positional matching, or refusing the destructive call.
- A supporting document whose path legitimately appears only in externalized text.
- A prior capsule so large that inlining it into prepare would breach the transport budget; the reporter's own phase is the realistic case.

tasks.title: Stop a checklist replacement silently destroying every tick
tasks.description:
The most damaging defect in this phase: a tool reports success while destroying durable state.

Current state: `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts:1614` handles a task update carrying a `checklist` array with

    if (checklist !== undefined) task.checklist = checklist.map((item, index) => ({ id: createChecklistItemId(task.id, index + 1, item), number: index + 1, title: item, checked: false }));

`checked: false` is hardcoded and nothing matches against the existing items. `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:1724` repeats the same construction independently, and `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts:1503` uses the same shape on creation (correct there, since a new task has no prior state). The call then returns `updated: true`.

Reported consequence: an agent in another project edited eight checklist titles through `planner-task-update` and lost all six ticks. It noticed only because a previous agent had written a warning into its handoff. Nothing in the result indicated loss.

Desired state: a checklist replacement never silently discards tick state. The input is a plain string array, so identity has to be reconstructed; decide deliberately between matching surviving items by exact title, matching positionally, or refusing the destructive call outright when it would clear ticks. Record the choice as a phase-owned Accepted Decision rather than leaving it implicit.

Implementation steps:
- Put the merge in plan-core, not in either adapter. Both adapters currently build this list themselves; after the fix neither should know how tick state is preserved. This is the same mistake P103(F005)/T408 corrected for reply shaping — see `packages/plan-core/src/handoff-reply.ts` for the shape to follow.
- Apply it to both `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts` and `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts`, and grep afterwards to confirm neither kept a private copy.
- If the decision is to preserve by title, an item whose title changed is a new item and starts unchecked; say so in the tool description so the behaviour is discoverable before the call rather than after.
- If any tick would still be lost, the result must say which items lost state. A success result that silently drops ticks is the defect, so a partial-loss case must be visible in the response.
- Review the neighbouring tool descriptions: they already steer agents toward `planner-task-checklist-toggle/add/remove` for granular edits. That guidance is right but did not prevent this, because the destructive path stayed available and silent.

Behaviors to preserve: `createChecklistItemId` shape and stable ids; per-task C{n} numbering; creation at `:1503` starting unchecked; `planner-task-checklist-toggle/add/remove` semantics unchanged.

Edge cases: a replacement that reorders items; a replacement that renames one item and leaves seven identical; duplicate titles within one checklist; an empty replacement array (clearing the list deliberately); a replacement on a task that has no checklist yet.

Verification: focused `@agent-plan/core`, `@agent-plan/mcp` and `@agent-plan/pi-adapter` builds and their suites. Add regressions proving that editing titles preserves ticks, that a renamed item behaves as decided, that an intentional clear still works, and that any lost tick is reported rather than silent. Per AGENTS.md rule 17, no full repository gate.

tasks.title: Validate supporting documents against the submitted content, not the rewritten one
tasks.description:
A correctly linked supporting document is rejected because the check runs after the body was rewritten under it.

Current state: in `refreshPhaseHandoff` (`packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts:3770-3790`), a body above `TARGET_HANDOFF_CONTENT_CHARS` is passed to `externalizeOversizedHandoffContent`, and `effectiveInput` is rebuilt with `content: externalized.content` — the truncated remainder, with the moved text now living in a generated `.planner/docs/` file. Validation then runs against that rewritten body at `:3795-3802`, and `validateHandoffContextSync` in `packages/plan-core/src/handoff-context.ts` asserts `input.content.includes(requested.path)` for every manifest entry.

So when an agent links a document and mentions its path in a section that externalization later moves out, the check fails against a body the path is no longer in, and `HANDOFF_SUPPORTING_DOCUMENT_INVALID` fires on a document that was linked correctly.

Reported by a peer session on 2026-09-15: the error demanded that the content link `.planner/docs/t474-library-capabilities-2026-09-15.md`, and that exact path was present in their "## Supporting documents" section. Their working theory was that the detector could not match a backticked path inside a list item. That theory is wrong — `includes` is a plain substring test and would have matched. The cause is ordering. Their workaround (remove the entry from the manifest, leave the path in prose) worked because the manifest is what triggers the check at all.

This is also a live cost: the failure happens at write time, so before P103(F005)/T409's retention it cost a full resend of the capsule. Retention now makes the retry cheap, but the rejection is still wrong.

Desired state: the "content must link this document" check is evaluated against what the agent submitted. Externalization is a planner-owned transformation applied afterwards and must not invalidate the author's own linking.

Implementation steps:
- Capture the submitted body before externalization and run the link check against it, or run the link check against submitted and externalized text combined. Either is defensible; pick one and say why in the code.
- Keep every other supporting-document check where it is. Only the body-dependent link check is affected by the rewrite.
- The planner-owned auto-externalized document appended at `:3788-3792` must continue to be exempt from agent-manifest defect reporting, as established by P103(F005)/T407.
- If the check still fails, the error should state which body it checked, so the next agent is not left theorising about backticks.

Behaviors to preserve: automatic externalization above the target; the 24,000-character ceiling; the typed `HANDOFF_SUPPORTING_DOCUMENT_INVALID` code and the droppable-field recovery text added by T407; write-time validation remaining the authority over prepare-time validation; exact rollback.

Edge cases: a document path that appears only in the externalized portion; a path appearing in both portions; a manifest entry for the auto-externalized document itself; a body just above the target so that externalization moves very little.

Verification: focused `@agent-plan/core` suite plus the existing handoff regressions. Add a regression reproducing the reported case — a manifest entry whose path sits in a section that externalization moves out — and prove the write now succeeds. Per AGENTS.md rule 17, no full repository gate.

tasks.title: Give prepare the whole prior capsule it asks the agent to reconcile against
tasks.description:
This is why a verified resume-ready handoff shipped missing context a cold agent needed.

Current state: the handoff protocol instructs "Reconcile every still-relevant detail from an existing handoff; do not append a competing handoff." What `handoff_prepare` actually returns is `audit.handoff`, the persisted body — which for any previously externalized handoff is the truncated remainder, with sections ending in `[Extended detail continues in the linked planner document.]`. `buildHandoffPrepareReply` in `packages/plan-core/src/handoff-reply.ts` bounds it further for transport and reports `existingHandoffLength` and `existingHandoffTruncated`, but neither inlines the externalized file nor names what was elided. `auditPhaseHandoff` in `packages/plan-core/src/handoff-context.ts` does not read `.planner/docs/` at all.

Reported by a peer session on 2026-09-15. Three sections of the prior capsule came back elided, one cut mid-word ("⚠️ **Ownershi"). Six facts were lost — two live code defects, a wanted setting, a current design document, a binding pair that had been conflated before, and a confirmed by-design behaviour a future agent must not "fix". Every one of them lived only in the externalized document. The previous handoff had carried them precisely because no task holds them. The agent composed a fresh capsule instead of reconciling line by line, and prepare made that the path of least resistance by handing back an elided copy. A human asking "are you sure it has full context?" is what caught it.

Their self-assessment called this "partly my fault". It is worth recording that the tooling asked them to reconcile against something it did not give them.

Desired state: an agent preparing a handoff can see everything the prior capsule carried, or is told exactly what it cannot see.

Implementation steps, in order of preference — pick one and record the choice as a phase-owned Accepted Decision:
- Inline the externalized text alongside the persisted remainder, budget permitting.
- Return the externalized document's content as a separate field so the caller can read it deliberately.
- At minimum, list the headings and the `.planner/docs/` paths that were elided, so the omission is visible rather than silent.

Whichever is chosen, the elision must never again be invisible to the agent doing the reconciling.

Also in scope: the split point. `externalizeOversizedHandoffContent` cut the reporter's body mid-numbered-list, moving "What is left" and half of two other sections into the file. A later rewrite at 7,996 characters was kept whole, so the threshold itself is fine — only the split is not section-aware. Make it break at a section boundary so neither half is left incoherent.

Behaviors to preserve: the 8,000-character capsule target and 24,000-character ceiling; automatic externalization; the payload reductions and no-duplication invariant from P103(F005), pinned by `packages/plan-core/test/handoff-reply.test.mjs` — a naive inline would breach both, so measure before and after; prepare-time supporting-document validation from T407; the candidate-then-verify contract.

Edge cases: a prior capsule whose externalized document alone exceeds the transport budget (the reporter's own phase is the realistic case); several externalized documents from successive rewrites; an externalized document that has been deleted from disk; a phase with no prior handoff.

Verification: focused core, MCP and Pi suites. Add a regression that externalizes a body, then proves prepare surfaces the moved content or names it as elided. Re-run the P103 payload assertions and record the new figures against the 18,033-character prepare baseline measured on heca P082. Per AGENTS.md rule 17, no full repository gate.

tasks.title: Replace the unchecked reconciliation boolean with something the planner verifies
tasks.description:
The only gate on the most loss-prone step in the handoff protocol is the author's own say-so.

Current state: `handoff_write` takes `reconciledExistingHandoff` as a boolean. The agent asserts it; nothing checks it. `validateHandoffContextSync` in `packages/plan-core/src/handoff-context.ts` does not compare the new content against the prior capsule in any way. An agent that composed a fresh capsule and never looked at the previous one passes this gate exactly as easily as one that reconciled line by line.

Reported by a peer session on 2026-09-15, whose verified resume-ready handoff dropped six facts the previous one carried. They asserted `true` in good faith. Nothing caught it; a human did.

The planner is in a position to do better. `auditPhaseHandoff` already parses the prior capsule and, once P104(F005)/T415 lands, will have access to its externalized portion too. It can therefore see the prior capsule's sections and compare them with what the agent submitted.

Desired state: reconciliation is evidenced rather than asserted. When sections present in the prior capsule are absent from the new content, the planner names them and the author accounts for each — deliberately dropped, superseded, or folded in elsewhere. A bare boolean should no longer be sufficient on its own.

Implementation steps:
- Derive the prior capsule's section headings during prepare and carry them to write, keyed to the prepare token so the comparison is against what the author was actually shown.
- At write time, list prior sections with no counterpart in the new content and require an explicit per-section disposition before persisting.
- Prefer a typed no-mutation outcome that names the unaccounted sections over a generic refusal, in the style of the existing `HANDOFF_PREFLIGHT_REQUIRED` and `HANDOFF_REASON_REQUIRED` codes.
- Keep the cost of complying low. P103(F005)/T409 retains the submitted body against the prepare token, so a refusal here should let the author supply only the dispositions on retry, without resending the capsule. Verify that actually works rather than assuming it.
- Do not make this a completeness audit. P100(F021)/T396 deliberately removed the 16-section scaffold and the 14-category inventory because they made authoring verbose and failed late. This must stay a narrow check — which prior sections vanished — not a return to that contract.

Behaviors to preserve: free-form concise capsules with optional headings (P100(F021)/T396, second pass) — a capsule with no headings at all must still be writable, so the check must degrade gracefully when the prior capsule had no section structure either; the 8,000-character target; the candidate-then-verify contract; body retention from T409.

Edge cases: a prior capsule with no headings; a deliberate full rewrite where every prior section is genuinely obsolete; a phase whose prior handoff was archived rather than superseded; a first handoff with nothing to reconcile against; a prior section renamed rather than dropped.

Depends on P104(F005)/T415: comparing against an elided prior capsule would reproduce the original defect, since the sections most likely to be dropped are exactly the ones prepare currently hides.

Verification: focused core, MCP and Pi suites. Add regressions for a dropped section being named, a per-section disposition satisfying the gate, a heading-free prior capsule still being writable, and a refusal followed by a retry that supplies only dispositions. Per AGENTS.md rule 17, no full repository gate.

tasks.title: Bound tool results and state payload limits before a call fails
tasks.description:
Diagnosing an oversized payload currently costs more context than the payload did.

Current state, both measured rather than reported:
- A successful `planner-task-update` in this session returned a 122,628-character result. The harness had to spill it to a file and the caller then needed jq to read back whether `updated` was true. The tool echoes the entire task — full description, every checklist item, the whole statusLog — when one field changed.
- A peer session on 2026-09-15 had a `description` of roughly 17,000 characters rejected, and the rejection came back as a 125,115-character tool result. Roughly 13,500 characters were accepted on a later attempt, so a limit exists but is nowhere stated.

The result is a tool that punishes the caller twice: once for exceeding an undocumented limit, and again for finding out.

Desired state: a mutation result says what changed, not what the entity now contains in full. The size limit is discoverable before a call rather than after it fails.

Implementation steps:
- Shape mutation results in plan-core so both adapters inherit the bound. `packages/plan-core/src/handoff-reply.ts` is the precedent from P103(F005)/T408: reply shaping lives in the core and both adapters render what it returns. Do not fix this in `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts` alone.
- Echo the fields named in `updatedFields`, plus identity and the freshness diagnostics, rather than the whole entity. A caller wanting the full entity can call the show tool.
- State the accepted size in the tool description, and make the too-large failure a compact typed outcome naming the field, its length and the limit — not an echo of the payload that failed. The existing `DESCRIPTION_MARKDOWN_FALLBACK_REQUIRED` path already tells callers to move long prose into `.planner/docs/` and pass a `descriptionRef`; that guidance should reach the caller in a few hundred characters, not a hundred thousand.
- `descriptionRef` was unusable until `packages/plan-core/src/payload-fallback.ts` was relaxed to accept three-segment paths (committed at a0ea1ba, unreleased). Two peer sessions wrote "do not retry it" into their handoffs. Confirm the fallback path now works end to end from both adapters, because the advice to use it is worthless if the field still refuses.
- Check `descriptionFreshness` and `staleParentRefs` on the update result: they are useful and should survive the trim.

Behaviors to preserve: `updated`, `updatedFields`, and typed failure codes must stay exactly as they are — mutation-integrity checking depends on them; `NO_MUTABLE_FIELDS_RECEIVED`; the description-fallback flow; the freshness preview contract.

Edge cases: an update that legitimately changes the description, where echoing the changed field is itself large — bound it and say it was bounded; a batch-shaped update touching several fields; a failure arriving before any field was parsed.

Verification: focused core, MCP, Pi and server suites. Add a regression asserting a successful update result stays under a stated ceiling for a task with a long description and a long statusLog, and that an oversized-field rejection is compact and names the limit. Measure a real `planner-task-update` result before and after and record both figures. Per AGENTS.md rule 17, no full repository gate.
